headline: CHINA EXTENDS RARE EARTH SUSPENSION TO JANUARY 10 — BEIJING ISSUES MOFCOM ANNOUNCEMENT No. 58
snippet: China's Ministry of Commerce issued Announcement No. 58 on November 9, extending six export-control suspensions — including those covering medium and heavy rare earths — through January 10, 2027. The extension preserves the trade truce struck after the 2025 Xi-Trump summit, but crucially does not lift the April 2025 licensing requirements for dysprosium, terbium and five other heavy rare earths that remain in force. Western buyers get another 60 days of relative supply security, but the January 10 date aligns directly with the Pentagon's DFARS magnet-sourcing deadline.

headline: GOLD SLIDES TO $4,053 (-2.1%) AS HOTTEST CPI IN MONTHS LOCKS IN DECEMBER HIKE — SILVER GIVES UP 2.8%
snippet: Spot gold ended the November 10 session at $4,053.30 per troy ounce, down $87.21 (2.11%) — its steepest single-day drop in weeks — after a hotter-than-expected October CPI print hardened December rate-hike expectations. Silver fell to $51.92/oz, off 2.80%, wiping out Monday's recovery. The pullback resets gold's near-term technical picture after a failed attempt to hold the $4,100 zone; with December Fed pricing firming, the focus shifts to whether the $4,000–$3,980 band holds before the next catalyst.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING Q3 RECORD GOLD PRODUCTION AND EARNINGS — KIDD ADDS BY-PRODUCT CREDITS AT $4,100 GOLD
snippet: Discovery Mining Corp (TSX: DSV) reported Q3 2026 results showing record gold production, sales and earnings — the first full quarter to include Kidd Operations (acquired June 1), which adds copper and zinc by-product credits alongside gold at $4,100+ metal prices. Exploration drilling at Owl Creek, where a 1.5 km underground drift from Hoyle Pond gives direct drill access, is advancing toward NI 43-101 resource estimates targeted for delivery before year-end — a potential near-term re-rating catalyst for the stock.

headline: USAR DELIVERS FIRST YTTRIUM OXIDE FROM WHEAT RIDGE — US DOMESTIC RARE EARTH SEPARATION DEMONSTRATED
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) announced delivery of first yttrium oxide samples from its Wheat Ridge, Colorado demonstration facility — a milestone in US domestic rare earth separation capability distinct from its Texas Round Top mine and Brazil Serra Verde commercial production. Yttrium oxide is used in LED phosphors, laser materials and specialty alloys; producing it from domestically-sourced feedstock closes a critical gap in the supply chain running from mine to finished materials, ahead of USAR's planned full-scale US processing complex.

headline: CRML BUYS 8% OF MORRO DO FERRO BRAZIL RARE EARTHS FOR $3.5M — US FIRM BETS ON NON-CHINESE SUPPLY
snippet: Nasdaq-listed Critical Metals Corp (CRML) is investing A$5 million (approx. US$3.5 million) in Power Minerals to secure an 8% stake in the Morro do Ferro rare earth project in Minas Gerais, Brazil — one of South America's most significant rare earth occurrences outside China's processing network. The move coincides with China's export control extension, as Western strategic buyers simultaneously secure short-term supply via the waiver while locking in direct project-level exposure in non-Chinese jurisdictions for the longer term.

headline: VALE BASE METALS CEO: ON TRACK TO TRIPLE EARNINGS TO $5B IN 2026 — COPPER AISC TURNS NEGATIVE
snippet: Vale Base Metals CEO Shaun Usmar says the subsidiary is on track to triple its earnings to approximately $5 billion in 2026, driven by record copper production (highest since 2017), all-in sustaining costs falling to negative territory on copper, and rising nickel output at sharply lower unit costs. The outlook positions Vale Base Metals as one of the world's strongest large-scale copper-nickel operations — contextually important as physical copper tightness in China drives record Yangshan premiums of $230/t.

headline: YANGSHAN COPPER SPOT GOES QUIET ON SHFE DELIVERY TIMING — ING WARNS CORRECTION MAY NOT BE OVER
snippet: Shanghai Metals Market reported sluggish Yangshan spot copper trade on November 10 as SHFE futures approach their delivery period, with holders reluctant to move metal ahead of settlement — a sharp contrast to Monday's record $230/t import premium. The divergence between headline premium strength and thin physical activity suggests demand urgency may have front-run rather than sustained the bounce; ING analysts flagged a continued LME correction risk even after last week's 2.7% decline.

headline: FOOL: WHERE GOLD AND COPPER GO FROM HERE — 3 MINING STOCKS TO OWN EITHER WAY AT $4,000 GOLD
snippet: The Motley Fool's November 8 analysis models two commodity bull scenarios — copper toward $16,000/t and gold holding the $4,000 floor — and identifies three mining stocks structured to outperform regardless of which path dominates, drawing on Newmont's Q3 average realized price of $4,317/oz as evidence that large producers are capturing the gold bull at record per-ounce margins. The framework — prioritizing lowest-quartile AISC producers with high commodity leverage — applies equally to smaller-cap juniors where operational leverage to gold is even greater than at the majors.

headline: GOLD MINERS 30-40% BELOW 2026 PEAKS WHILE METAL HOLDS $4,100 — ANATOMY OF OCTOBER'S SELLOFF
snippet: Discovery Alert's November 2026 analysis quantifies why gold miners remain 30–40% below their 2026 peaks despite gold trading near $4,100/oz: October's risk-off wave hit juniors and silver producers hardest as ETF outflows overwhelmed the fundamental case, pushing the GDX/GDXJ discount to bullion to its widest since 2016. The piece identifies three structural reasons the discount persists — operational leverage cuts both ways, capital return programmes are nascent, and institutional coverage of junior names is thin — offering a framework for investors deciding whether to add on weakness.

headline: PENTAGON'S JANUARY 2027 MAGNET DEADLINE APPROACHES — WHAT THE 0.1% DFARS RULE MEANS FOR RARE EARTH SUPPLY CHAINS
snippet: Carra Globe's analysis unpacks what the January 2027 timeline means for rare earth supply chains beyond China's extension: US DFARS rules require that by January 2027, magnets in defence equipment contain no more than 0.1% Chinese-sourced rare earth content. With the Pentagon's $2 billion critical minerals stockpile commitment and the DFARS cliff arriving simultaneously, the piece identifies which domestic rare earth projects — including USAR, MP Materials and Lynas USA — are positioned to meet defence qualification timelines and which face disqualifying gaps in separation or metal production capacity.
